name: Cidra (Puerto Rico, United States)
description: A brown vertical stripe at the hoist of about a third of the length, and a fly divided horizontally green over yellow, charged with the municipal seal in a black-edged white ring.
history: Cidra is a town and municipality in central Puerto Rico, the "Town of Eternal Spring". The gold stands for the richness of its fruits and waters, the green for its year-round green landscape and the brown for the Virgin, the town's patron, and the plain pigeon; the flag, arms and seal designed by Professor J. J. Santa-Pinter were approved by the Municipal Assembly under decree No. 8 of the 1975–76 series on 25 September 1975.

features.role: municipal seal in a white ring edged in black, reading CIDRA PUERTO RICO
